Chillers must not be shut down routinely.** Per the chiller manual and SOP-02, chillers stay on over weekends and maintenance because **burn-in rooms and the server room still need cooling** [source: docs/knowledge/equipment/EQ-07_chiller.md#EQ-07 Chiller Manual > Shutdown] and [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > What stays on over the weekend]. Yes, the demand was too high on 16 June.

On 2025-06-16, the plant hit a peak of **1324.4 kW** at **08:15**, which is **6% above** the 1250 kW contract limit [data: get_demand]. Two 15-minute intervals exceeded the contract:

- 08:00 → 1307.1 kW
- 08:15 → 1324.4 kW (peak) [data: get_demand]

This is the "Monday morning simultaneous start" scenario (S2): demand climbed from ~310 kW overnight to a spike as the SMT lines and reflow ovens started at once [unverified citation removed]. The exceedance was caught by the monitoring system as a "demand above contract" detection, with a penalty impact of NT$11,819.88 over 2 intervals [unverified citation removed].

A staggered start (15 min apart) would have lowered the peak to 1187.7 kW and avoided the full penalty [unverified citation removed].

I have all the information needed from the plant documents.

## Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby

A reflow oven in **standby still draws 36% of its 70 kW rating — about 25.2 kW per oven** for the entire time it is left on [source: docs/knowledge/equipment/EQ-01_reflow_oven.md#EQ-01 Reflow Oven Manual > Energy-saving notes]. That is a large idle load while the line produces nothing, so SOP-02 requires the ovens to be switched **fully OFF** at the end of the working week, not left in standby [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]. A correctly shut-down oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend, versus the standby oven's full draw [source: docs/knowledge/equipment/EQ-01_reflow_oven.md#EQ-01 Reflow Oven Manual > Shutdown].

## Excess energy in incident S5

During incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), RF-02 was left in standby all weekend:

- Standby weekend energy: **≈ 1,556 kWh**
- Normal weekend energy: **≈ 346 kWh**
- **Excess: ≈ 1,210 kWh** from that single oven [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

Note that the off-schedule rule would only flag this after 120 minutes above 20% of rating, so the real benefit comes from switching the oven off proactively rather than detecting it afterward [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

## Load Shedding Order (SOP-03)

**Shed first:** EV charging is the first action.

| Order | Action | Equipment | Share of present load |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Pause EV charging** | EV-01 | 100% |
| 2 | Delay the next burn-in loading | BI-01, BI-02 | 35% |
| 3 | Raise chilled-water setpoint +1 °C | CH-01, CH-02 | 4% |
| 4 | Lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar | AC-01, AC-02, AC-03 | 3.5% |

So **EV-01 charging is shed first**, followed by burn-in loading, then chilled-water setpoint, and finally compressed-air pressure. You stop as soon as projected demand is back under contract. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order]

**Loads that must never be shed:**
- The server room
- Running molders mid-cycle
- Reflow ovens with boards inside

This is confirmed in both SOP-03 and the energy policy. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order] and [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-01_energy_policy.md#EM-01 Energy Policy > Operating principles]
